A.objective: From authoritative data-room sources, determine which represented billed revenue (invoices) is associated with counterparties whose active contracts contain acquisition-relevant conditions, and report each qualifying invoice with counterparty and contract identifiers as they appear in the sources.

entities_in_scope: counterparties named on invoices and contracts
exclusions: expired statements of work (not active contracts)
invoices not linked to a counterparty with an active contract bearing acquisition-relevant conditions

world_true: invoice identity and billed amount, currency, period, status as recorded in billing sources
contract identity and counterparty naming as recorded in contract sources
contractual clause text and its literal content
contract effective dates and statement-of-work expiry status as recorded in sources
purpose_analytical: active contract vs expired statement of work (purpose threshold on contract liveness)
acquisition-relevant condition present vs absent (purpose classification of clause kinds)
invoice-to-contract association asserted vs unresolved (purpose epistemic disposition on joins)

epistemic_requirements: Report invoice-to-counterparty/contract association only when confidently supported by source evidence; otherwise mark association as unresolved.
Missing identity linkage is not a negative contractual finding: do not omit an invoice solely because join confidence is lacking, and do not assert a join without confidence.
Contract identifiers and billed names must appear as they appear in authoritative sources (no silent canonicalization in output).
Acquisition-relevance judgments must be grounded in explicit contractual language, not inferred from counterparty similarity or commercial notes alone.

allowed_unresolved_states.meaning: A billed invoice is represented, but the invoice billed name cannot be confidently associated with a contract counterparty and governing contract.

must_include: every invoice that qualifies under purpose policies (active contract with acquisition-relevant condition) with association asserted
every represented invoice for which acquisition exposure is under review but invoice-to-contract join cannot be confidently made, with association unresolved
must_not: treat unresolved identity as proof that no acquisition-relevant contract exists
drop invoices silently when joins fail
completeness_expectations.receipt: Output is complete over represented billed revenue subject to purpose inclusion rules when every in-scope invoice appears once in the invoices array.

acquisition_relevant_conditions: requires consent or notice on a change of control
permits termination upon a change of control
requires consent or notice before assignment, including assignment restricted except to affiliates, or assignment prohibited to a competitor
purpose_specific_policies.active_contract_rule: An expired statement of work is not an active contract; only active contracts create acquisition exposure for this purpose.
purpose_specific_policies.inclusion_rule: Include an invoice row when it is associated (asserted or unresolved) with a counterparty whose active contract contains at least one acquisition-relevant condition.

association_dispositions.asserted: Confident that the billed name corresponds to the contract counterparty and the stated contract_id governs the relationship.
association_dispositions.unresolved: Cannot confidently associate billed name with contract counterparty; report rather than omit or assert.

not_world_truth: The label acquisition-relevant is an analytical policy for diligence, not a contractual term of art in the sources.
The active contract threshold for this purpose may be stricter or different from raw contract metadata fields.

B.objective: From authoritative data-room sources, identify represented customer and commercial identities across CRM, billing, the company registry, and contracts; for each commercially relevant name or record, report whether it can be confidently treated as the same legal counterparty as other records, or whether identification remains unresolved.

required_output_shape.ordering: sort links by left ascending, then right ascending

world_true: distinct source records and their native identifiers
legal names and company numbers as recorded in registry
CRM account names and billed names as recorded
contract counterparty strings as written in contract files
purpose_analytical: same legal entity vs distinct entities vs unresolved (purpose identity judgments)
mechanical legal-form variant vs substantive distinct registry entity (purpose merge policy)
commercially relevant record vs out-of-scope record (purpose scope filter)

epistemic_requirements: Do not globally merge records merely because two names look similar.
Exact legal-form variants of the same registered name may be treated as mechanical sameness when confidently supported.
Distinct registry entities with similar trade names are not automatically the same party.
Missing a positive same-entity judgment is not a negative judgment: absence of SAME_ENTITY does not imply DISTINCT.
Every required connecting link among CRM account, billed name, governing contract, and registry candidate must appear explicitly with an epistemic disposition.

allowed_unresolved_states.meaning: Insufficient evidence to assert SAME_ENTITY or DISTINCT for the left/right pair.

must_include: every link required to connect a CRM account, its billed name, the contract governing that relationship, and any registry row that is a candidate legal entity for that relationship
must_not: collapse unresolved pairs into SAME_ENTITY by default
omit candidate links because reconciliation is hard
completeness_expectations.receipt: Output is complete when all commercially relevant cross-source identity links demanded by the purpose are present with an explicit epistemic value.

merge_policy.permit_mechanical: Exact legal-form variants of the same registered name (e.g., punctuation or suffix differences) may be SAME_ENTITY when mechanically derivable.
merge_policy.forbid_similarity_merge: Similar trade names or fuzzy string match alone is insufficient for SAME_ENTITY.
merge_policy.distinct_registry_entities: Separate registry rows remain DISTINCT unless positive same-entity evidence exists.

purpose_specific_policies.required_link_pattern: For each commercially relevant relationship, connect crm account, billing billed name, governing contract identifier, and registry candidate(s) via directed left/right pairs.

epistemic_dispositions.SAME_ENTITY: Confident the two identifiers denote the same legal counterparty.
epistemic_dispositions.DISTINCT: Confident the two identifiers denote different legal counterparties.
epistemic_dispositions.UNRESOLVED: Cannot confidently decide sameness or distinctness.

not_world_truth: SAME_ENTITY/DISTINCT/UNRESOLVED are diligence identity judgments, not entries in a global canonical entity table.
Identifier prefix conventions (crm:, billing:, etc.) are output rendering rules for this purpose, not source-native IDs.

C.objective: From authoritative data-room sources, compute a commercial dependency view: identify counterparties that are commercially dependent under purpose-defined criteria, listing open invoices, governing contracts, obligation kinds, and dependency status.

identifier_forms.note: Same identifier forms as Purpose B

required_output_shape.ordering: sort dependencies by contract_id ascending; obligation_kinds sorted within each row

world_true: invoice open/closed status as recorded in billing sources
contract text for exclusivity, auto-renewal, and rolling-term clauses
contract effective and expiry dates as recorded
counterparty naming on contracts and invoices
purpose_analytical: current commercial relationship vs historical-only (purpose liveness threshold)
commercially dependent vs not dependent vs unresolved (purpose composite judgment)
obligation kind classification: exclusivity, auto_renewal, rolling_term (purpose taxonomy)

epistemic_requirements: If identity needed to join invoice and contract is unresolved, report the dependency as unresolved rather than as false (not dependent).
Dependency status=dependent requires both prongs of the purpose dependency test to be confidently satisfied.
Use Purpose B identifier forms for counterparty fields; unresolved identity from B propagates as unresolved dependency here.
Expired contracts do not create current dependency regardless of past invoice history.

allowed_unresolved_states.meaning: A candidate dependency cannot be asserted because invoice-to-contract/counterparty identity join is unresolved, or other required evidence for the two-prong test is missing.

must_include: every counterparty-contract pair that satisfies both dependency prongs with status dependent
candidate dependencies blocked by unresolved identity joins with status unresolved
must_not: mark status dependent when identity join is unresolved
treat expired-only or one-off historical paid invoices without active contracts as current dependency
completeness_expectations.receipt: Output is complete when all in-scope commercial dependency rows are reported with explicit status and sorted obligation_kinds.

dependency_test.prong_1_current_relationship: There is a current commercial relationship: an open invoice, OR an active contract that auto-renews or continues on a rolling term.
dependency_test.prong_2_obligation: The active contract contains an exclusivity commitment, OR a term auto-renewal, OR a rolling term that continues unless notice is given.
dependency_test.conjunction: Both prongs must hold for status=dependent.

exclusions.expired_contracts: Expired contracts do not create current dependency.
exclusions.historical_one_off: A one-off paid historical invoice without an active contract does not create dependency.

obligation_kinds.sorting: obligation_kinds list must be sorted ascending within each dependency row

status_dispositions.dependent: Both prongs satisfied and identity joins sufficient to assert dependency.
status_dispositions.unresolved: Dependency cannot be confidently asserted or denied because required joins or evidence are unresolved.

purpose_specific_policies.cross_purpose_dependency: Relies on Purpose B identity reconciliation for counterparty identifier joins; unresolved B links force unresolved C status rather than negative dependency.
not_world_truth: Commercially dependent is a diligence analytical label, not a legal term defined in contracts.
Current relationship and active contract thresholds are purpose-specific and may differ from raw source status fields.
